articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Three-level Diode Clamped and T-type Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: In this paper, the 3-level Diode-Clamped (Neutral Point Clamped) inverter and the T-Type multilevel inverter topologies are studied relative to each other. Based on a number of performance metrics, such as switching frequencies, modulation index, and total harmonic distortion (THD), a comparison is made. Pulse generation is achieved by means of the Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM) technique. To examine their impact on THD and RMS Voltages for both inverter types, differing the switching frequencies and modulation index is done. A T-type inverter uses a T-type topology, which is distinguished by its more straightforward structure, whereas a Diode-Clamped inverter uses diodes to accomplish multiple voltage levels. In order to create a sinusoidal output, the inverter's switching pattern can be precisely controlled by selecting the SPWM mode.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for Loan Approval Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: The financial sector of any nation is the key factor in elevating the economy of nation. The biggest issue that finances departments are facing is to approve loans for valid candidates only. Our proposed model for predicting the loan approval for valid candidates uses three different supervised learning algorithms for classification of loan approved or not, on the basis of candidate attribute values. In proposed study ensemble technique has been used to find out best classifier algorithm to train our model. In this paper we are comparing KNN, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, SVC, and Naïve Bayes classifier algorithms based on their accuracy for provided data set to find out the highly accurate and efficient algorithm for designing a model for approving loan to valid candidate which will also help in minimizing the financial frauds.

articleTitle: Beamforming and Phased Arrays: Elevating MIMO-OFDM Systems for Next-Generation Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This study explores the optimisation of Multiple Input Multiple Output-Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems through the use of phased arrays and advanced beamforming methods. With a focus on overcoming the challenges that come with 5G wireless communication, like high data rate needs, interference resistance, and efficient spectrum usage, this work presents a novel approach that combines dynamic beam steering and adaptive precoding to significantly enhance system performance. Through thorough modelling, we demonstrate considerable improvements in bit error rates (BER), throughput, and spectrum efficiency compared to traditional MIMO-OFDM configurations. The results demonstrate a 25% improvement in throughput and a 40% reduction in BER in densely populated metropolitan environments, underscoring the potential of phased arrays and beamforming to further improve 5G network performance. This work not only validates the efficacy of the proposed enhancements but also establishes a foundation for future advancements in wireless communication systems by highlighting the critical roles that phased arrays and beamforming will play in achieving the maximum potential of 5G technology.

articleTitle: Real-Time Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Communication refers to exchanging information between two people to perform different tasks or develop bonding for personal or professional use. Effective communication provides a lot of advantages in terms of business meetings and gatherings. It is quite easy for normal people without these disability to communicate with each other but there is a major problem of communication for deaf people all over the world. Sign language is a major source of communication for deaf people, but the problem arises for normal people to communicate with them, so sign language acts as a source of communication for them. A model for the recognition of various gestures has been designed for this problem. LSTM (long short-term memory) model has been proposed for sign language recognition. The model is designed in a way that it can take input from the user through the webcam which has been made with the help of datasets fed with the help of OpenCV which has been trained to recognize the datasets through labels set on them. The output of the software is that the user can thereby see the meaning of the symbol or signs that has been performed in front of the webcam. This model can be quite effective in terms of exchanging information between deaf and mute people and normal people.

articleTitle: Design, Modelling, and Performance Comparison of Five-Phase PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: In today’s electrical industry, Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) are replacing Induction Motors due to their numerous advantages such as high-power density, high efficiency, and reduced torque ripple. Reliability is crucial in high-power applications like aerospace, electric ships, machine tools, wind power generation, and electric vehicles. Multi-phase machines, especially multi-phase PMSMs, are well-suited for these applications due to their high fault tolerance capability and reliability. However, the commercial production of multi-phase machines is not yet widespread due to their high manufacturing cost. To address this, it is necessary to develop a model and perform its analysis using finite element analysis to reduce manufacturing costs, material wastage, and expert’s time. This approach helps to create better products and reduce total production costs. This paper discusses the design, mathematical modelling, development, and performance of a five-phase PMSM. The development process uses finite element analysis-based ANSYS MAXWELL software, while mathematical verification is done using MATLAB Simulink. The performance characteristics obtained from MAXWELL and MATLAB models are compared and verified.

Author Keywords: five phase permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: DDoS Landscape: Insight into Attacks and Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Cyberattacks have become a common occurrence in every corner of society where the Internet has spread. With almost all of the businesses online, nefarious people are finding it more incentivized to carry out attacks against these online entities. DDoS attacks have emerged as one of the most powerful and popular cyberattacks in the recent past. Continually evolving defense tactics have resulted from their extreme devastation combined with their ease of execution. In this paper, we provide a basic architecture of DDoS attacks and discuss a few popular DDoS tools available online. We carry out a case study in which we investigate the characteristics of malicious packets generated by different tools as a reference for DDoS detection systems.

articleTitle: Analysis and Performance Evaluation of a 14 nm Junctionless ⊥-FinFET Biosensor for Biological Species Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the design, simulation, and performance analysis of a cutting-edge 14 nm junctionless ⊥-FinFET biosensor tailored for the detection of biological species. In this paper, on both sides of the fin, a 4nm of nanocavity is designed. This nano cavity has been formed between the gate to the fin for settling the biomolecules. Biomolecules are introduced into the device's cavity and nanocavity to facilitate immobilization. Subsequently, the performance characteristics of the device, including the switching ratio, and threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) shift, are meticulously investigated utilizing a TCAD (Technology Computer-Aided Design) device simulator tool. This analysis is conducted with the primary objective of detecting the presence of biomolecules. Different biomolecules such as Streptavidin, K=2.15, Aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES), and Keratin, K = 8 are considered for investigating the capability of biosensors. The electrical characteristics of the biomolecule examines and compared with without biomolecule and with neutral charge molecule, with positive charge, and with negative charge particle. The proposed device investigates the device's electrical characteristics, sensitivity, and detection limits, demonstrating its potential for highly efficient and accurate biosensing.

articleTitle: Intelligent Traffic Management System: An Advanced Solution for Helmet Compliance, Traffic Signal Violation Detection, Number Plate Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) is an advanced solution that aims to enhance road safety by ensuring helmet compliance, detecting traffic signal violations, and identifying number plates. This system utilizes cutting-edge technologies such as computer vision, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to monitor and analyse various aspects of traffic. One of the key features of the ITMS is its ability to enforce helmet compliance. The system will be able to determine if riders are wearing helmets or not, by analysing real-time video footage from surveillance cameras using computer vision algorithms. Furthermore, the ITMS incorporates traffic signal violation detection capabilities, providing an efficient solution for identifying and penalizing motorists who disregard traffic signals. This helps in reducing accidents and improving overall traffic flow. Another important functionality of the ITMS is number plate identification. Through optical character recognition algorithms, the system can capture and extract license plate numbers of vehicles passing through specific checkpoints. In summary, the Intelligent Traffic Management System offers a comprehensive solution for ensuring helmet compliance, detecting traffic signal violations, and identifying number plates using YOLO v7 Algorithm. With its integration of advanced technologies, it provides an efficient and effective approach to enhance road safety and traffic management.

articleTitle: Navigating the Landscape: A Comprehensive Review of State-of-the-Art Traffic Detection Approaches and Unveiling Open Research Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Traffic management is crucial for the smooth flow of vehicles on the roads. Automation in traffic management requires computerized mechanisms for detection of vehicles. With the continuous increase in vehicle population, traffic congestion has become a global issue these days. This has a negative influence on people's lives because of things like the increased commute time, health related issues due to environmental pollution, decreased social life, etc. A significant amount of research has been suggested on this subject to lessen the negative consequences of congestion in our life. Researchers all around the world are paying close attention to the Intelligent Transportation System (ITS), one of the prospective solutions that could enable a variety of applications to enhance travel comfort and safety. Accurate traffic detection is one of the most important issues that must be resolved in ITS to effectively manage the transportation system and alleviate traffic congestion. This survey attempts to provide a thorough overview of the state-of-the-art proposed traffic detection approaches to create the groundwork for understanding the open research challenges in traffic detection.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Technology for Microbial Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: One benefit of electricity generation directly in a microbial fuel cell (MFC) from waste biomass is that it can produce high-columbic efficiency green energy. The output voltage and power density of the Microbial Fuel Cell are quite low, even though it can produce green energy from waste. The output voltage ranges from 300mV to 800mV and its power density is around 100 – 2000 mW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Meanwhile, most electronics devices require above 3.3 V to operate. Therefore, there is a need to boost this output voltage and power to usable levels for electronic devices. Therefore, this paper proposes various energy harvesting technologies to raise the voltage of MFC to usable form. Future work will concentrate on creating a power management system (PMS) with ultralow power consumption components that is optimized for MFC operation.

articleTitle: Exploring Diverse Logic Implementations and Full Adder Circuit Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: In the last few years scientists are more focused towards in the reduction of the chip size and on the low power consumption of the chips in VLSI design. In digital electronics there is a digital circuit called as full adder generally which is used in the addition of two bits in various devices. In this paper there is a review of various full adders by using different logic styles such as CMOS(Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor), CMOS Domino Logic, Emitter-Coupled Logic, Pass Transistor Logic and Transistor-Transistor Logic. It operates very fast and uses very little power. In this paper there is a comparative study of various Full-Adders by using different techniques to show the results for the technique which is better for carrying out of Full-Adder Circuit in digital electronics. Here in this all the full adders which is taken for the review are simulated on 45-nm of technology. The parameters which are compared here is Delay(pS), Power(uW) and PDP or Power Delay Product(aJ). In all the full adders which are discussed in this paper XOR and XNOR transistors are used. Here in this paper simulation results are also added which is of HPHFA full adder. Here in this paper it is observed that HPHFA full adder 10.3-40.5% and 10.7-45.9% is better in terms of delay and PDP.

articleTitle: The Impact of Cloud Computing on Data Science and Engineering: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This paper delves into the dynamic relationship between cloud computing and data science and engineering, emphasizing the significance of scalability, cost-efficiency, and collaboration in advanced analytics and innovation. Tracing the historical evolution of cloud computing, it highlights challenges like data security and governance while predicting its integration with cutting-edge tech. Emphasizing the transformative potential, the study underscores the imperative for businesses to harness cloud computing for sustainable growth and innovation, offering insights into emerging trends and best practices.

articleTitle: Strengthening Cloud Security For Unauthorized Access Prevention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Due to the increased frequency of recent attacks, there are serious cyber security issues as a result of smart device usage. Cloud computing has brought about major changes in the commercial world. Centralization, however, increases the danger of important data breaches and makes it impossible to deploy dispersed services like security systems due to the massive volume of data that is transmitted between businesses and cloud service providers. Insider attacks are a serious risk to the business since they can cause more damage and have greater access. Finding different strange events that could point to anomalies and security issues with privilege escalation is the aim of this technique. Through the use of ensemble learning to combine multiple models, the strategy can improve machine learning outcomes and prediction performance. The proposed standard uses a modified dataset taken from the CERT dataset to assess the Support Vector Machine (SVM) machine learning technique for insider attack classification. Utilizing patterns of behavior and activity, such as resource usage, file access times, and login times, the system builds a profile of typical behavior and looks for deviations. This strategy can assist companies in identifying insider threats early on and avert serious harm to their priceless resources and data.

articleTitle: Design of CMOS Voltage Reference Circuit using LDD MOSFETs in BCD 110nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This work presents a voltage reference that uses lightly doped drain MOSFETs to achieve a low area and low sensitivity. The circuit operates within the voltage range of 0.98V to 2V for the minimum supply voltage and maximum supply voltage. This circuit has a temperature coefficient of 61.02 ppm/°C. This circuit has a line sensitivity of 0.042%/V. The area of the chip is 0.000309 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The design has been simulated using Cadence Virtuoso and ELDO simulator tool for 110nm BCD technology and the layout of this circuit is completed using Cadence Virtuoso tool and Mentor Calibre for physical verifications.

articleTitle: Using Image Processing and Machine Learning To Identify Plant Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: The use of machine learning and image processing techniques for plant disease diagnosis is explored in this research. We compare various disease classification algorithms and frameworks and do a thorough study of prior research. This analysis highlights the benefits and limits of current approaches by diving into the accuracy attained in detecting various plant ailments. Also included is an analysis of the difficulties faced and potential solutions to these problems within this rapidly developing field.

articleTitle: Estimation of Respiratory Rate Using Facial Video Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: The Respiratory rate (RR) is a crucial indicator of health, often used to detect respiratory and cardiac conditions. Traditional RR measurement methods can be intrusive and uncomfortable. The work explores a non-contact method for estimating RR using video analysis. By detecting facial features and analyzing intensity variations in the chin region, it demonstrate that video-based RR estimation is a feasible and effective alternative to conventional methods. The findings suggest significant potential for applications in telemedicine, remote health monitoring, and continuous patient assessment.

articleTitle: Unveiling Prognostic Pattern: A Hybrid Approach For Predictive Analytics in Medical Image Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Currently, medical image data are being processed using deep learning technology to revolutionize disease-related research. Deep learning-based medical image analysis involves the application of various essential tasks, including medical image reformation, enhancement of image quality, segmentation, classification, and Computer-Aided Detection (CAD). These tasks aim to discern differences between healthy cells and tumour cells, facilitating more accurate diagnoses and effective treatment planning. This paper focuses on employing a hybrid approach for medical image analysis, integrating both clustering and classification techniques. The proposed methodology leverages k-means clustering, Visual Geometry Group (VGG), and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) on distinct datasets related to cardiovascular diseases, breast cancer, and brain diseases. The hybrid approach aims to capitalize on the strengths of both clustering and classification methods, enhancing the overall accuracy and interpretability of the medical image analysis process. By utilizing diverse datasets, the research endeavours to contribute valuable insights into the identification and understanding of various diseases, ultimately advancing the field of medical image analysis for improved healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Analytical Study of Pre-trained Transformers in Natural Language Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: The paper presents an overview of how conversational agents have evolved over time from rule-based to complex models of NLP to address issues in creating an agent that understands the user's intentions and responds in a natural way. How these different applications of machine learning, deep neural networks, and reinforcement learning helped to maintain the contexts, understand the languages better, generate responses with ethical considerations are discussed hereafter for improving the user experience. This paper contributes valuable insights into the field of AI chatbot development by fusing existing technologies with future opportunities and manages to come out with a pathway for innovations further down the track of conversational AI.

articleTitle: Parametric Comparison of Linear-ion Drift and VTEAM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Memristors, as a new electronic component, have unique properties such as non-volatile memory and a unique pinched hysteresis loop in their voltage-current characteristics. However, precisely simulating the nonlinear ion drift dynamics of memristor presents a substantial challenge. These devices are well-known for their non-volatile applications because of the pinched hysteresis loop with non-linear behavior. This paper outlines the I-V characteristics of the linear-ion drift model and VTEAM models by changing the frequency and voltage parameters. By observing the acquired results, in the linear-ion drift model, it is extremely difficult to generate a non-linear i-v curve while retaining memristance behaviour at high frequency and voltage ranges. The reason for this drawback could be due to the lack of threshold value in this model. So, to address this issue while maintaining the PHL (Pinched hysteresis loop) at a specific threshold level, the VTEAM model was implemented.

articleTitle: Animal Classification Using Cnn Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This study addresses the problem of wild animal attacks and disappearance in areas such as farms or villages near forest and mountains, proposing a solution through deep learning algorithms. Using deep learning architectures, specifically convolution neural networks (CNNs), the study intends to accurately identify and classify animals based on categories. The dataset has been taken from Kaggle which consists of 90 different animal images, employing various CNN architectures those are LeNet-5, AlexNet, VGG16, ResNet50, Inception V3, and InceptionResnetV2. along with that implemented techniques such as data augmentation to fix the problem related to lack of data and, we used techniques like dropout to tackle the problem related to the model overfitting. The Study paper compares and analyses the accuracy of these algorithms, contributing to comprehensive understanding of their efficiency. Furthermore, different performance metrics are used names as accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score are used to check the accuracy and the model effectiveness. Furthermore, we have explored related works in automated classification and object detection, particularly focusing their application on animal classification. The results highlight the potential of deep learning in forest to create some sort of alert system or create a system which can provide information on endangered animal or rare animal.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Disease Classification through Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Study and Model Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This research tackles the pressing need for precise lung disease classification using deep learning models on chest X-ray images. Lung ailments pose a global health challenge, demanding accurate diagnostic tools to ease healthcare burdens and enhance patient outcomes. Traditional methods, often reliant on subjective human judgment, introduce potential errors and inefficiencies. The study centers on employing advanced deep learning models like DenseNet, MobileNet, ResNet, and ChexNet to automate classifying various lung diseases. Recognizing the complexities and variations in pulmonary conditions, the research aims to elevate diagnostic accuracy. It contributes to ongoing efforts to refine lung disease classification methods and bridge existing accuracy gaps. Through a comprehensive exploration of diverse deep learning models and their modifications, the study demonstrates improvements in model performance, indicating the potential for tailored modifications to address the intricacies of different lung diseases. The paper discusses the significance of the study in advancing automated diagnostic tools, providing insights into the relationships between specific diseases and deep learning models. The emphasis is on the adaptability and nuanced approach required for robust lung disease classification.

articleTitle: A Web Traffic Data Analysis System based on Statistical-Analytical Report Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: To increase the business value in terms of quality of service, it is quite necessary to have aspects of the performance of the system. The website ownership always demands to perform certain analysis so that they can get maximum profit through their business. However, conducting meaningful data analysis requires a proper understanding of the data’s narrative and/or interpretation as numbers alone do not make any sense. Improper understanding of data could result in wrong output. To overcome this, specialized knowledge and expertise is the possible solution. Therefore, the authors created an automated system for analyzing web traffic data from mobile devices and web. The descriptive statistical-analytical techniques had been utilized in the report-generation process, but now the system employs a technique called Bootstrap Aggregator to automatically identify customer needs and generate data analysis reports. Furthermore, the researchers compared the output reports generated by two different algorithms: Deterministic Linear Decision Tree (DLDT)-for analytical and Random Forest-for automatic. Their findings have revealed that both algorithms produce reports with a high degree of user satisfaction and acceptance.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Bone Injury Diagnosis with Advanced Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This research delves into the critical issue of detecting and classifying bone fractures using advanced image analysis techniques. Accurate and timely identification of bone fractures is essential for effective treatment, given their prevalence and significant impact on patient recovery. Early detection plays a crucial role in reducing complications and enhancing overall healing. The study utilizes a dataset of 4,906 X-ray images, divided into two categories: fractured and non-fractured. A Sequential Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is applied, achieving an impressive 98% accuracy in fracture classification. This is based on a training set of 4,099 images, a testing set of 401 images, and an additional 406 images for validation. The results underscore the effectiveness of deep learning in medical imaging for accurate and efficient fracture diagnosis, showcasing its potential to enhance healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Feature Map Guided Strategy for Robust Multi-Resolution Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Presence of haze in digital images poses significant challenges in computer vision applications, adversely impacting tasks like image segmentation and object detection. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces a fusion-based dehazing strategy by integrating color conversion, adaptive gamma correction, and parameter estimation. Through multi resolution fusion of chromatic and brightness maps, the algorithm efficiently removes haze, surpassing conventional single-image approaches while maintaining computational efficacy. From comparative analysis it is evident that, the proposed strategy is highly effective in terms of improving image quality for diverse applications.

articleTitle: Lazy Merge Sort: An Improvement over Merge Sort
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Arrangement of elements in a dataset often forms a crucial aspect in determining the overall performance of the underlying algorithms. Elements arranged in sorted order, either ascending or descending, may serve as an additional benefit for many other algorithms to work upon efficiently. Many algorithms exist in the literature for sorting of the data. The algorithms have wide range of applicability depending on their distinctive properties. However, O(nlogn) algorithms are frequently used in most of the real-world languages and applications. This research aims to further optimize the already existing Merge Sort. It proposes a modified approach named as Lazy Merge Sort that works on the principle of deferred merging until the last step by creating in-between sorted sub-arrays. The proposed approach is further validated and analysed over O(nlogn) baseline algorithms. During the experimentation and validation phase, the proposed Lazy Merge Sort performed better as well as proved to be efficient with respect to other baseline algorithms. The average and worst time complexity for the proposed algorithm is O(nlogn) and traditional Merge Sort serves as an upper bound for it. It offers a competitive alternative to conventional methods and contributes significantly to sorting algorithms in Computer Science.

articleTitle: Dual-Model Approach for Diabetic Retinopathy and Macular Edema Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) and Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) are major causes of vision loss in diabetic patients. Early detection is crucial for preventing permanent vision impairment. This research paper proposes a novel dual-model architecture for detecting Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema. The proposed framework integrates preprocessing techniques such as circular cropping and Ben’s preprocessing, followed by data augmentation. The Diabetic Retinopathy model is trained on the APTOS2019 dataset, while the Diabetic Macular Edema model is trained using the IDRid dataset. InceptionV3 outperforms other models with an accuracy of 88% for Diabetic Retinopathy classification, while MobileNetV2 outperforms other models with an accuracy of 83% for DME classification. The dual-model architecture enables simultaneous evaluation of retinal images for DR and DME diseases. The Experimental results demonstrate promising outcomes, suggesting the potential effectiveness of the proposed dual-model architecture in diagnosing diabetic eye diseases.

articleTitle: CNN-Driven Innovations in Dysarthria Classification and Speech Disorder Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This research article addresses dysarthria, a speech disorder frequently observed in individuals with cerebral palsy (CP) or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Early detection of dysarthria is essential for effective treatment and improved patient outcomes, as it significantly impacts communication abilities. Utilizing the TORGO database, which comprises 2000 speech samples from both dysarthric and non-dysarthric individuals across various genders, this study employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for classification. The dataset includes 500 samples each from both groups, collected in different sessions. The CNN approach achieves an impressive 96% accuracy in distinguishing dysarthric from non-dysarthric speech, showcasing the potential of deep learning technology in facilitating early dysarthria diagnosis and enabling timely interventions. This study makes substantial contributions to enhancing diagnostic capabilities and offers a promising avenue for improving the quality of life for individuals with speech disorders.

articleTitle: Federated Learning Approaches for Enhanced Chinese Text Classification Across Diverse Domains
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This work assesses the advancement achieved in cross-domain Chinese text categorization through implementing FL. Audible, explicit, and traditional methods of centralized text categorization present severe privacy and security concerns because all the data is gathered at one server location. FL solves these problems by enabling the model training on multiple devices while keeping data locally. The trials have proved that the FL framework we proposed achieved a better performance than traditional centralized and domain-specific models, having an accuracy rate of 88. 4%, compared to 83. 7% and 86. 0% respectively. They suggest a 4. 7% and 2. 4% increase, respectively. In other words, the proposed framework obtained the FL model with the micro-average precision, recall, and F1-score of 88. 2%, 88. 1%, and 88. 0% respectively. The results show good generalization over virtually any domain, whether data or features. The approaches using differential privacy and secure multi-party computing achieved high accuracy rates of about 88%. 1% while Ordinary Least Squared achieved 90%, but secure multi-party computation reached the highest 88%. 2%. This proves that it is possible to balance the high accuracy of the tests and the protection of the individual's data. The evaluation of the training time of the FL framework and the computational load of the framework showed that the FL had a training time of approximately 5. There is no change in hours and inference times of 24 ms per instance that can be compared to standard models. Moreover, regarding the communication cost, the FL framework has a price of merely 10 MB per communication cycle.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fabrication Techniques for Thin Film Schottky Diode for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Thin film technology is made of material ranging from nanometers to micrometer in thickness. Thin film technology was developed to cater the needs of the IC industry. High demand for thin films compatible with high speed devices has introduced us to updated fabrication technologies. Knowledge of properties of thin nano-films and electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, capacitors can be shall be used for future communication technologies and devices. A review of different fabrication techniques is discussed in this paper with their superiorities and limitations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Health Monitoring and Telemetry Integration for CubeSat’s Onboard Computer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This paper delves into the development and implementation of a Health Monitoring and Telemetry Subsystem (HMTS) specifically designed for CubeSat’s Onboard Computer (OBC). Through extensive academic research, the study emphasizes the importance of proactively tackling power failure scenarios by implementing a data- driven approach. This involves implementing real-time health monitoring, fault detection, and logging to ensure a robust system. The study highlights the practicality of using the Arduino Uno simulator to validate code and discusses potential future endeavours related to cross-compilation on the Raspberry Pi OBC. Thorough research conducted in the academic field has shown that implementing a proactive maintenance strategy significantly improves the durability and performance of CubeSat missions.

articleTitle: AI Based Drive Cycle Prediction for HEV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: HEVs (Hybrid Electrical Vehicles) is regarded as one of the most effective solutions in the context of environmental pollution and fuel consumption. Nevertheless, formulating the sustainable Energy Management Strategies (EMSs) for HEVs is not an easy task while at the same time one has to meet different design objectives and achieve maximum fuel economy. Among numerous EMSs, the present paper highlights the new system of AI-powered Driving Cycle Prediction. Using the Machine Learning Algorithms and Time Series Forecasting, we apply Dynamometer Drive Schedules data for EVs, meanwhile, Mean Squared Error (MSE) helps to evaluate the model quality. XGBoost and NBeats algorithms comparison shows that the last one has much higher forecasting accuracy; however, it is computationally heavier. Such study is focused on the development of HEV technology and hence the availability of sustainable transport solutions through the process of providing detailed information on the algorithmic outputs.

articleTitle: Empowering E-commerce: Leveraging Open AI and Sentiment Analysis for Smarter Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Online product reviews are pivotal in shaping consumer purchasing decisions in today's digital era. Leveraging the wealth of sentiment-rich data available through these reviews, this research proposes an approach to enhance product recommendation systems. This study integrates sentiment analysis techniques into the recommendation process to provide users with more personalized and insightful product recommendations. By analyzing the sentiment expressed in user-generated content, such as reviews and ratings, this system aims to capture not only the explicit preferences but also the underlying sentiments and emotions of users towards products. Furthermore, this system utilizes OpenAI and the power of Langchain to develop a chatbot interface, enabling users to interact naturally and receive personalized product recommendations based on their preferences and sentiment analysis. Through experimentation on real-world datasets, this paper evaluates the effectiveness and performance of the sentiment-enhanced recommendation system compared to traditional recommendation methods. The results demonstrate the potential of sentiment analysis in improving the relevance, accuracy, and user satisfaction of product recommendations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of GCN and GAT for Predicting Protein-Protein Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) play a fundamental role in biological activities. However, accurately predicting PPIs remains challenging due to the complexity of protein interfaces and the vast number of potential interactions. To address these challenges, this study explores the use of graph attention networks (GATs) and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to predict PPIs. These deep learning architectures excel at handling graph-structured data, representing proteins as nodes and their interactions as edges. By leveraging various data sources, including sequence and structural data, GCNs and GATs aim to improve prediction accuracy. Ultimately, these advancements hold significant implications for drug discovery, vaccine development, evolutionary biology, and protein function annotation. The curated PPI Dataset can be found at: https://github.com/PrayujS/PPI-Prediction-using-Graph-Nets

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency in Cs2CuBiCl6 Solar Cells through Minimizing Interface Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Conventional perovskite suffers from PV performance and stability issue. To address above issues, we have optimized the perovskite based solar cell through novel material. In this work we have utilized the Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CuBiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> material as an active layer owing to its inexpensive cost, exceptional optical qualities, low-temperature coefficient, direct bandgap characteristics, and extraordinary stability. SCAPS-1d have been utilized for the simulation where interface defect density (IDD) of the active layer have been varied and best PV performance has been recorded. The study highlights the output of the Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CuBiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> based PV cell, as the output of the result is remarkable that is about to PCE of 8.44%, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> 0.35 V, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> of 33.02 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and FF of 71.76% is obtained. Based on these results, Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CuBiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> emerges as a highly prospective candidate for the advancement of PV technology.

articleTitle: Data Protection Strategies: Employing IBBE and Attribute-Based CPRE for Secure Data Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Worldwide, people and businesses are starting to adopt cloud computing more and more. Although there are still many issues that need to be overcome, cryptography can assist users in public clouds in protecting their data. We present a practical and safe identity-based data group sharing and distribution system for public clouds that enables data owners to simultaneously broadcast encrypted data to multiple recipients. Security issues with public cloud infrastructure are the driving force behind data confidentiality regulations. We employ conditional proxy re-encryption that is both ascribe-based and timed-release, which gives the cloud server a reencryption key. These ways, only disseminators whose characteristics comply with the encrypted data's access policy are able to distribute it to other groups beyond the release period. Through this, we are able to disseminate data groups in a secure and adaptable manner. The distribution of cipher texts can be controlled by data owners with fine-grained and timed-release access control by re-encryption conditions that are connected to characteristics and release time.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cardiovascular Health through AI-Driven Heart Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Early detection of heart issues thanks to AI working hand in hand with cardiovascular health. This method reliably predicts the risk for CVDD by SVM model, which have been proven consistent classification accuracy and also can maintain all information of high dimension data. The model was trained and validated on an extensive dataset of controlling significant clinical and physiological interpatient variability. In order to ascertain those medical diagnostics, become as reliable as possible, the performance of the SVM is evaluated with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and some other suitable metrics. The proposed model had a prediction accuracy of (96.5%) which is significantly better than existing benchmarks reflecting a significant improvement in the quality of care. With the capability of artificial intelligence (AI) to transform medical diagnostics and improve patient outcomes and the cost of healthcare. The paper demonstrates a new standard in clinical diagnostics through their analysis to provide credibility of AI-driven tools for the prompt detection and treatment of cardiovascular sicknesses with learn curves and confusion matrices, which are comprehensively performed.

articleTitle: Next Word Prediction System using NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This research paper introduces a novel statistical trigram language model designed for text prediction tasks, implemented using the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK). The model is trained on the renowned “Alice in Wonderland” corpus, leveraging a weighted random probability approach to predict the subsequent word in a provided phrase. A distinctive feature of this model is its user-controlled prediction termination, allowing individuals to determine when the prediction process should halt. To ensure data quality, the text undergoes rigorous preprocessing stages, eliminating superfluous characters and ensuring standardized tokenization into trigrams through NLTK’s robust capabilities. The research not only presents the predictive model but also includes comprehensive n-gram statistics, offering insights into the underlying linguistic structures. Additionally, a visually informative frequency distribution plot showcasing the top 30 most common trigrams enriches the analysis, aiding in understanding the corpus’s textual patterns. This paper contributes to advancing text prediction methodologies by combining statistical modeling, NLTK proficiency, and user interactivity, offering a valuable tool for language enthusiasts, researchers, and developers alike.

articleTitle: A Study on Multifactor Biometrics Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: With the recent advancements and rise in technological applications, information security and privacy are the most prioritized domains in which people are concerned about. Be it a governmental institution or a small business firm, all their relevant data is being stored online and exposed to cyberattack in the digital world. Authentication using biometrics has been considered as the most suitable method owing to its universality, uniqueness, acceptability, and performance. However, relying solely on a single mode authentication system (referred to as Unimodal Biometric System) may prove inadequate in ensuring privacy and security of digital data. Hence, it has become essential to use multiple biometric modalities in verification/authentication systems. Multimodal biometric or multifactor biometric system consists of more than one physical or behavioral trait as an additional layer of protection for authentication of confidential data. present paper provides a brief account of three multimodal biometric systems and a comparison based on their experimental results. Here, the integration of the biometric traits is accomplished using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approach, where facial recognition has been fused with other biometric traits in order to achieve the most accurate match for its implementation in real world applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Visual Cryptography scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Visual cryptography schemes (VCS) are essential for safe communication and image transfer. Nevertheless, pixel enlargement is a common problem with traditional VCS, which can hinder practical implementation by increasing storage and transmission cost. In this research, a unique method for creating robust, visual cryptography schemes (VCS) that prevent pixel expansion is presented. Our suggested systems take advantage of sharing and modification encoding techniques to make them small without sacrificing security. Through the optimization of pixel utilization and the application of sophisticated cryptographic techniques, our strategy minimizes data redundancy while upholding the encryption concept.

articleTitle: IoT based Smart Fall Detection Device for Elderly People
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Instances of falls, especially among the elderly, pose notable health concerns, prompting the need for innovative interventions. This paper presents an inventive approach to fall detection via the development of a wearable smart device. By harnessing Internet of Things technology and an advanced sensor array, our system aims to improve the precision and efficiency of fall detection while prioritizing user comfort. The proposed device seamlessly integrates into daily life, providing non-intrusive monitoring. Through the utilization of accelerometers, gyroscopes, and various sensor technologies, the system captures and assesses pertinent data related to human movement patterns. This data is then processed using an Internet of Things framework, enabling real-time communication and alert generation in the event of a fall. To validate the efficacy of our wearable smart fall detection device, extensive testing and evaluation have been carried out. The research focus includes assessing the device's sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy in distinguishing authentic falls from routine activities. The results illustrate the system's potential to deliver swift and precise fall detection, thereby facilitating timely assistance and minimizing the repercussions of falls.

articleTitle: Speed Control of an In-wheel brushless DCmotor using PID controller for EV’s
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: In recent years, electric vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a sustainable and eco-friendly transportation option. A key factor in the performance and efficiency of EVs is the precise control of the electric motor driving the vehicle. This study introduces a robust speed control methodology for in-wheel brushless DC (BLDC) motors in EVs using a proportional integral-derivative (PID) controller. In-wheel motors offer numerous advantages such as improved vehicle dynamics, increased energy efficiency, and simplified drivetrain architecture. However, precise speed regulation is essential to optimize performance and ensure vehicle stability, particularly in varying operating conditions. The proposed PID controller is designed to address the inherent challenges of in-wheel BLDC motor control, including nonlinearities, disturbances, and dynamic load variations. Through systematic tuning and optimization, the PID controller ensures accurate speed tracking with minimal overshoot and settling time. Simulation studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the control strategy across a range of operating conditions, including acceleration, deceleration, and steady-state cruising. The experimental results confirm the ability of the PID controller to maintain precise speed control under different driving scenarios, highlighting its potential for enhancing the performance and efficiency of electric propulsion systems in next-generation electric vehicles and the prototype will be implemented

articleTitle: Dynamic Container Optimization for Efficient Microservices Deployment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This study presents a novel technique to Dynamic Container Optimization that aims to improve the deployment efficiency of microservices in cloud settings. The strategy uses a heuristic technique for intelligent microservice-container pairing and is focused on reducing operational expenses, guaranteeing Quality of Service (QoS) compliance, and resolving the container cold start issue. By methodically choosing the best matches between microservices and containers, the algorithm reduces resource waste and maximizes CPU and memory usage. To address the issue of cold starts in containers, the study also suggests a reusability method for containers that is predicated on predetermined principles and strategically identifies warm containers. The algorithm's thorough performance analysis demonstrates consistent resource utilization, quick processing times, and substantial cost-effectiveness, highlighting the Dynamic Container Optimization technique as a viable answer to the changing microservices deployment challenges in dynamic cloud environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Text-Independent Speaker Verification through Advanced Deep Representation Feature Analysis with Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Speaker Verification (SV) identifies individuals II. RELATED WORK by evaluating their distinctive vocal qualities. Text-independent speaker authentication is an important task in speech recognition and security applications. This proposes an extended fine-grained analysis of deep representation features for text-independent speaker verification using neural networks. This paper uses a Combination of CNN and RNN Neural Network Models for verification. Two Machine Learning Models Random Forest Classifier and AdaBoost Classifier was implemented on speaker verification system, but the neural network model outperforms both the models. The model achieves the accuracy of 96.4%. The approach has numerous practical uses across different security and access control systems, as well as in speech recognition technologies.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Advancements in Patient Pain Detection using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This review provides a systematic overview of the current state of sentiment analysis as applied to detecting pain from facial expression A key feature of this work is the employment of an analytical framework informed by PRISMA guidelines, Our research consisted of an extensive search of multiple high-profile databases for all articles published within the last five years. In light of selection criteria which rejected articles devoid of any machine or deep learning techniques for gaining knowledge of pain through facial expressions. To select the approximate papers, our evaluation process applied a strict set of inclusion/exclusion criteria. In addition, focus was placed on methodology, Datasets, feature extraction approaches, classification, evaluation metrics, etc. A critical approach was used that compared the advantages and disadvantages of each of the methodologies. However, to achieve the goal of improving patients’ outcome, one must be aware of the threats listed above and would be prepared to apply the suggested innovations to sentiment analysis for pain detection. Ultimately, this approach is likely to help make this tool much more important for healthcare professionals, which would bring more benefits for pain management and patient care.

articleTitle: Study of Failures in Continuous Integration Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery (CD) is a strategy for faster and high-quality software delivery. CI brings many advantages in software industries, quick detection of bugs when integrating code, faster integration and release time. However, it also comes up with its own challenges to meet organization expectation of being robust and continuously run throughout the project development cycle. It emphasizes that all failures in the CI process, whether genuine software bugs, test failures, or CI tools-related issues, play a critical role in increasing the delivery time of software. The basic aim is to raise awareness of these often-overlooked factors and argues for their equal importance in the context of CI and CD strategies for achieving faster, high-quality software delivery and help organization identify common issues in their CI/CD pipeline as well as make improvements to streamline the process and delivery of software in defined deadline. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the various non-softwa-rerelated failures that occur within CI environments and propose a Pram model that shows promising improvement to mitigate such failures.

articleTitle: Real Fake Image Classification using Explainable EfficientNetV2S: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This paper investigates the Explainable EfficientNetV2S model's ability to distinguish between authentic and counterfeit photos in order to social protection. By carefully organizing the data, as well as by creatively using explainable images, study analyze the activation layer-wise results of EfficientNetV2S on actual and false image datasets. This study use both traditional CNN and transfer learning technology with a dataset split 80% for training and 20% for testing, with a particular emphasis on the robust EfficientNetV2S pretrained on ImageNet. Metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and categorical losses are all included in this study, which shows that EfficientNetV2S significantly improves performance. It outperforms the conventional CNN model with remarkable accuracy of 98.99% and validation accuracy of 97.81%. This study’s result shows that the EfficientNetV2S discriminate the fictitious and original images in efficient and effective manner and resulting in advancements in authenticity verification and image classification.

articleTitle: Optimizing Network Intrusion Detection with Hybrid DTRJ Model: A Data Mining Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This research delves into the development and implementation of the Hybrid Decision Tree-based Random Forest and J48 (DTRJ) Model for network intrusion detection, employing a data mining approach to significantly enhance feature selection and classification algorithms. With the burgeoning complexity of cyber threats, traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) face challenges in effectively monitoring and securing networks. Leveraging the NSL-KDD dataset, this study introduces sophisticated data preprocessing and feature selection methods, including the Modified FireFly Algorithm (MFFA), Chi-square, and Bayes Network, to refine the detection process. The core of the research is the Hybrid DTRJ Model, an innovative ensemble classifier that merges the strengths of Decision Tree-based Random Forest and J48 algorithms, aiming to improve detection accuracy and minimize false positives. A comprehensive performance evaluation using various metrics confirms the model's effectiveness in identifying network intrusions, setting a new benchmark for IDS efficiency and reliability. This research highlights the critical role of advanced data mining techniques in the future of network security, offering a robust solution to adapt to and mitigate evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: Analyzing Awareness and Adoption of E-commerce and Online Transactions in Rural India: Bridging the Digital Divide for Rural India
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: These days, e-commerce and online transactions are spreading quickly throughout our nation. It has a significant impact on India's digitalization. In this study, we will examine rural residents' awareness of online transactions and e-commerce. Online transactions and ecommerce contribute to the development of Digital India and the economy. The goals of this study's strategies are to determine and analyze the proportion of individuals in underdeveloped areas who use e-commerce websites to buy and sell goods, as well as how many of them are aware of online transactions and e-commerce and use payment methods like cards, UPI apps, net banking, and wallets. A questionnaire is used to gather all of this data. The answers provided in relation to residence, age, income, gender, occupation, and other factors are used to analyze the study's results. This study will assist in providing the appropriate analysis of the results of our survey work as well as the results for research work discussion.

articleTitle: Gamification: The Effective way for better learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Gamification is a blooming technology that transforms stereotypical academics into interesting game-like elements. Through gamification, educators motivate the students to involve themselves in the game design for entertainment and adopt the features of the game design in an educational setting for enhanced learning. This work focuses on an educational digital game for learning sorting algorithms and concepts from data structures. The game is designed based on constructivism learning theory and the MDA framework, aiming to promote active and student-centered learning. The game challenges players to rearrange a sequence of unsorted aliens by using a set of commands, such as comparing, swapping, and moving. The game also records players’ actions and performance through log data, which can be analyzed for learning behavior, and outcomes. It describes the game design and development process, as well as the potential benefits and limitations of using the game in computer science education, and also discusses how the game can facilitate the development of computational thinking skills such as problem formulation, abstraction, algorithmic thinking, and generalization.

articleTitle: Plasmonic-Mode Driven Graphene Metasurface Perfect Absorber with Wide Frequency Agility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)

authors.preferredName: K. S. V. S. V. Phaneeth

abstract: This work presents a graphene-based tunable metasurface absorber (TMSA) with an absorption efficiency of 99.96% at 1.65 THz. The DC biasing of graphene sheets helps to achieve frequency tunability from 1.2 to 2.65 THz. The proposed TMSA is compact and ultra-thin, having a periodicity and thickness of $\frac{{{\lambda _0}}}{{22.73}}$ and $\frac{{{\lambda _0}}}{{90.9}}$, respectively, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is calculated at 1.65 THz. An acceptable A(f) response has been achieved for the variation in polarization (ϕ) and incidence (θ) angle. These features enable the deployment of the TMSA for radar cross-section (RCS) reduction and stealth/defense applications in the THz regime.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 3D-Printed ASA Substrate based Antenna for Wi-Fi 6E Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This paper presents a first attempt to employ a 3D-printed substrate antenna for Wi-Fi 6E applications. The substrate is fabricated using Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate (ASA) filament and is characterized in terms of its dielectric constant and loss tangent using the ring resonator method. A wideband antenna, designed to operate within the Wi-Fi 6E frequency band (5.925 to 7.125 GHz), is rigorously analyzed through simulations conducted with Ansys High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software. The proposed wideband antenna features dimensions of 32 mm × 27.5 mm with tapered edges and a partial ground structure. It achieves a S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> below -10 dB across a frequency range of 5.175 GHz to 9.345 GHz, ensuring wideband performance. The simulation and experimental results are in well agreement, highlighting the feasibility of the ASA as a 3D-printed substrate for Wi-Fi 6E communication systems. It is significant to evaluate ASA's suitability for antenna applications due to its exceptional weathering, UV, and chemical resistance, along with ease of processing, enabling reliable and customizable antennas.

articleTitle: Parkinsons Disease Progression Prediction using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition that affects people over time and significantly lowers their quality of life. Patients with PD experience both motor and non-motor symptoms. Through clinical evaluation, the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) is used to quantify the severity of Parkinson's disease. No definitive diagnostic tests for PD currently exist. Emerging machine learning techniques show potential to forecast future UPDRS scores for making informed medical decisions and enable better disease management. This paper studies research leveraging proteomic data to forecast PD prognosis, focusing on advanced machine learning techniques like CatBoost Regressor, ElasticNet, XGBoost Regressor, RandomForest Regressor, ExtraTrees Regressor and DecisionTree Regressor.

articleTitle: Optimizing Rose Leaf Disease Detection Performance via Explainable Transfer Learning: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: This paper advocates a novel method for identifying disorders in rose leaves by applying transfer learning techniques. The methodology includes data collecting and preparation steps like reshaping, gray scaling, resizing, and augmentation. Initially, a basic Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is utilized, followed by pretrained transfer learning techniques on ImageNet. Specifically, DenseNet201, EfficientNetB3, InceptionResNetV2, and MobileNetV2 are used. The analysis is performed based on categorical losses, recall, accuracy, and precision. It is evident from comparing the experimental results to the CNN model's baseline that transfer learning greatly increases accuracy, precision, and recall. Applying CNN transfer learning models to the DenseNet201 architecture produces the best results, with accuracy of 94.41%, precision of 96.18%, recall of 92.77%, and validation accuracy of 98.91%. The outcome of DenseNet201is also visually analyzed through layer wise explainability. Results show the effectiveness of transfer learning and how its improving the CNN model's ability to diagnose diseases in rose leaves. Proposed study particularly promotes automated disease identification in plants in the field of rose leaf diseases. The findings offer valuable information for managing plant health and agricultural activities in future.

articleTitle: Design of 4×4 Circularly Polarized Phased Array MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Automotive Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: In the recent advancements in the wireless communication, 5G provides the reliable, uninterrupted and improved channel capacity signals throughout the communication while travelling and for users in rural areas. Therefore, phased array antenna with beamforming capability will be the one of the prominent solutions to address these features and ensure the effective communication. This paper describes and analyze the 4×4 slotted patch antenna array along with beamforming capability. The design provides the excellent impedance matching in Sub-6 GHz frequency bands dedicated for the 5G communication. The proposed array provides the gain of 18.5 dB which confirms the significant improvement in data rate according to link budget calculations. The beamforming feature of the proposed design demonstrates the -30° to +20° beam shift with the feeding phase shift of -30° to +40°. The specifications and performance of the design are suitable for various automotive wireless 5G use cases.

articleTitle: Enhancing Driver Safety with Transfer Learning based Deep Learning Models for Drowsiness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: In response to the escalating concern over road accidents due to driver drowsiness, this research delves into enhancing drowsiness detection systems using advanced deep learning techniques and transfer learning. Prior investigations have explored conventional methods, yet they often lack the precision demanded by real-world scenarios. Leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs) alongside model fine-tuning and transfer learning, our methodology aims to optimize drowsiness detection accuracy. Through rigorous experimentation, we achieved compelling results, showcasing significant enhancements in accuracy across various CNN architectures. For instance, with Max Pooling and 2 Dense layers, one of our CNN models achieved an accuracy score of 1 at epoch 2, with a remarkably low loss of 6.622934e-12, all while taking only 2.6648 seconds for training. These outcomes underscore its potential to revolutionize driver safety systems, offering promising avenues for future research and implementation in real-world contexts.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid CMOS Full Adder with Low Power and High Speed for Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: A low-power and high-speed CMOS (Complimentary Metal Oxide Semiconductor Logic) complete Full adder core is suggested for embedded systems in this work. This novel hybrid Full adder design consists of two different logic styles which is named as static CMOS logic and the pass-transistor logic, the present full adder digital circuit is based on a new three-input exclusive OR (3-XOR) design. Here in this novel full adder design the primary goal of this circuit is to provide the driving capability in addition it also gives the fast speed and low power consumption. The experimental circuit's properties, when compared to previous literature, demonstrate that the novel adder improves power consumption by 3.6% to 32.8%, time delay of Co by 10.9% to 40.6%, and power-delay product of Co by 12.9% to 90.9% by using the TSMC CMOS 0.35-µm technology which is also suitable for Mixed-Signal circuits. Out of all the Full adders which are chosen here for the comparison, the circuit has been shown to have the lowest consumption of power and there is a quickest carryout signal response. The new hybrid full adder and the XOR logic can be effectively integrated in an embedded system or SoC because of their high speed as well as where the low power consumption requirements are there in the circuits. This hybrid CMOS full adder uses a combination of PMOS and NMOS transistors to achieve low power consumption, high speed, and area efficiency. The sum and carry circuits are designed to implement the respective logical functions using a mix of pass transistor logic and traditional CMOS techniques. The resulting full adder is well-suited for embedded systems where power and speed are critical factors.

articleTitle: Solar PV and wind energy fed 4 kW DC Nanogrid With Light Electric Vehicle Load
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV’S) are the productive step to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and it also constitute to the major part of the present DC load demand and transport sector as well. Therefore, the development of EV’S charging infrastructure is also very important at the same time. DC charging station using renewable energy sources (RES) is significantly promoted in order to reduce the dependency on grid power and to achieve a cleaner and healthy environment. This paper outlines the design of 4 kW hybrid renewable energy fed DC charger for light electric vehicles. Perturb & Observe(P&O) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm has been applied to get the maximum power output from renewable energy sources. Phase shift control scheme designed using Proportional-Integral (PI) controllers and algorithm has been employed to the DC-DC phase shift full bridge (PSFB) converter to step down the 380V DC bus voltage to 48V to charge an electric vehicle battery. The system has been implemented on MATLAB/SIMULINK software to evaluate the results of the alleged system.

articleTitle: Voltage Control in Low Voltage Distribution Systems Using Smart Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Voltage stability is crucial for a reliable power supply, and smart converters offer effective solutions. They use advanced control algorithms for real-time adjustments based on grid conditions. Remote monitoring and control capabilities allow operators to manage grid data, responding promptly to voltage fluctuations. This work presents an optimal voltage control method which is implemented using smart power converter. The optimization method is solved using exhaustive search method. The results are obtained for a case study considering the worst-case scenario of 100% penetration of photovoltaic (PV) power without load demand in CIGRE low voltage residential distribution network. The Performance indicators include the voltage rise margin, voltage drop margin, and total load bus voltage deviation are calculated to show the effectiveness of optimal control method when compared to based case.

articleTitle: Oorja: Real-Time Sustainable Power Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: The significant increase in energy demands in the last decade has led to unnecessary usage of energy. Though the environmental impact of overconsumption of energy is not immediately observed, they do cause power plants to generate more carbon emissions annually. An effective solution needs to be identified to address these issues. Real-time energy monitoring could have a positive impact on society and the environment while laying the groundwork for a sustainable future. This paper proposes ‘Oorja’ - a real-time sustainable power monitoring system, which is a cost-effective and visionary solution designed to enhance energy efficiency. It is built using an ESP32 microcontroller with a PZEM-004T sensor. It is IoT-enabled to provide real-time monitoring and analysis of power consumption through a web dashboard, mobile app, or a dedicated receiver. With extensive safety features, such as a glass fuse, a high-pitched alarm, and an automated power cutoff, the proposed system allows homes and businesses to optimize energy use and save expenses without sacrificing safety. These measures are designed to prevent electrical hazards. Additionally, it has a special debug mode that allows the user to quickly troubleshoot any minor faults without involving an expert. Results in this paper demonstrate the realtime performance of the proposed system with a variety of devices acting as loads.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning and Machine Learning Models for Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Disease Classification from Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Worldwide, 33.9 million individuals have Alzheimer’s disease (AD), with prevalence projected to quadruple in 40 years. Adequate AD diagnosis is essential for prompt therapy. This study compares machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) strategies for AD classification using neuroimaging data obtained from the Kaggle Open Access Collection of Imaging Studies dataset (N=7839). This work tests ML and DL algorithms for AD classification using neuroimaging data. Preprocessing MRI data, data augmentation, model training, and performance assessment utilizing accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are the steps. ML algorithms like Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP are compared. Deep learning architectures like EfficientNetB3, EfficientNetV2S, MobileNetV2, NASNetMobile, and ResNet50 are also evaluated. Random Forest had the greatest accuracy (92.58%) and F1-score (0.824) of the ML models tested. ResidentsNet50 has the greatest accuracy of 99.75% on the original dataset, whereas EfficientNetB3 has the best validation accuracy of 95.16%. The work emphasizes method and model selection based on application needs such as precision, computational efficiency, and interpretability vs. accuracy for effective AD diagnosis using ML and DL approaches.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Voice-Enabled Web Application for Customer Interaction Using Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Web accessibility is crucial for inclusivity, particularly for users with diverse needs. This paper explores the integration of Dialogflow, a conversational AI platform, with Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Speech-to-Text (STT) technologies to enhance web accessibility. Our study aims to improve user interaction and accessibility features through this integration.
